description: Na₂LiCuP₂O₇ crystallizes in the monoclinic C2 space group. There are two inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded to five O atoms to form distorted NaO₅ trigonal bipyramids that share corners with five PO₄ tetrahedra and corners with two equivalent NaO₅ trigonal bipyramids. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.24-2.46 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.26-2.88 Å. Li is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to four O atoms. There are a spread of Li-O bond distances ranging from 1.93-2.33 Å. Cu is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to three O atoms. There are a spread of Cu-O bond distances ranging from 1.88-2.41 Å. There are two inequivalent P sites. In the first P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one PO₄ tetrahedra and corners with three equivalent NaO₅ trigonal bipyramids. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.53-1.64 Å. In the second P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one PO₄ tetrahedra and corners with two equivalent NaO₅ trigonal bipyramids. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.53-1.62 Å. There are eight inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to two equivalent P atoms. In the second O site, O is bonded in a bent 120 degrees geometry to two equivalent P atoms. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Na, one Li, and one P atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Cu, and one P atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to three Na, one Li, and one P atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Li, and one P atom. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Li, one Cu, and one P atom. In the eighth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Na, one Cu, and one P atom.
